scope_allowed: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

models.name: TRSB-FE: Thread-Resolved Screw–Bone Model
models.what_it_computes: Implicit nonlinear contact and damage simulation capturing thread flank engagement, insertion and stripping torque, axial pullout force–displacement behavior, and local bone stress/strain distribution.

models.name: HTA-FE: Homogenized Trabecular Anchor Model
models.what_it_computes: Implicit continuum model with anisotropic elastic–plastic trabecular surrogate and interface elements to predict anchor stiffness, early micromotion under bending, and degradation under cyclic off-axis toggling.

mechanisms.name: Monotonic axial pullout resistance
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Dominant extraction failure that governs fixation retention following implantation and during acute postoperative loading.

mechanisms.name: Thread stripping at peak insertion torque
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Loss of thread purchase during insertion compromises fixation and correlates with early loosening risk.

mechanisms.name: Off-axis toggling–induced loosening
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Repetitive cranio-caudal and medial–lateral moments at the screw–bone interface degrade purchase under physiologic motion.

mechanisms.name: Early micromotion under physiologic bending
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Small displacements at the anchor reflect purchase quality and influence construct stability during healing.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–9 Credibility Index (0=minimal evidence, 9=compelling evidence) for each model × mechanism pair.

spans: The TRSB-FE model predicted peak force with 12% mean absolute percentage error across n = 24 cadaveric anchors (RMSE 112 N; R2 = 0.86).
findings.span: The TRSB-FE model predicted peak force with 12% mean absolute percentage error across n = 24 cadaveric anchors (RMSE 112 N; R2 = 0.86).

spans: For monotonic axial pullout resistance, TRSB-FE achieved high ratings for mathematical structure and numerical realization because it explicitly resolves thread flank engagement and reproduces peak force with 12% mean absolute percentage error and R2 = 0.86 across 24 cadaveric anchors; input quality was strong because parameters were mapped from donor-specific imaging and independently measured friction coefficients, with only two global coefficients tuned from foam controls.

findings.mechanism: Thread stripping at peak insertion torque
spans: Across 28 insertions, peak torque error averaged 10% mean absolute percentage error (R2 = 0.82).

Seven insertions exhibited stripping; TRSB-FE correctly identified six of these based on a combined criterion of torque drop exceeding 15% and local plastic strain localization around the last engaged thread.
The receiver operating characteristic yielded an area under the curve of 0.84 for classifying strip versus non-strip cases based on simulation-predicted criteria.

spans: Under off-axis toggling (±5 N·m, 1 Hz, 10,000 cycles; n = 16), HTA-FE predicted loss of anchor stiffness with 14% mean absolute percentage error (R2 = 0.81) and micromotion growth per 1,000 cycles with RMSE 11 µm, whereas TRSB-FE yielded 22% mean absolute percentage error (R2 = 0.58; RMSE 19 µm per 1,000 cycles).

TRSB-FE, which can represent cyclic damage, produced 22% mean absolute percentage error (R2 = 0.58) for stiffness loss and micromotion growth RMSE 19 µm per 1,000 cycles; while trends were captured, cumulative error and computational cost were higher.

spans: Cyclic degradation reduced both strength and stiffness as S(N) = S0*(1 + N/Nc)^(beta), where beta = 0.18 and Nc = 3,000 for our loading amplitude, consistent with observed stiffness loss of 38% ± 16% at 10,000 cycles in cadaveric toggling tests.
